knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper presents a theory for simultaneous QED and QCD resummation to achieve 0.67% theoretical precision for LHC luminosity processes. This framework is derived from an exact rearrangement of the QCD perturbative series and is illustrated using single heavy gauge boson production.

attributes.purpose: simultaneous resummation of multiple gluon and photon radiative effects
attributes.implementation: Monte Carlo methods on an event-by-event basis
attributes.property: exact rearrangement of perturbative series without double-counting

relationships.target: single W, Z production with decay into light lepton pairs

attributes.basis: N=1 term in the exponent in the formal proof of exponentiation in non-Abelian gauge theories in the eikonal approximation
attributes.status: exact rearrangement of QCD perturbative series

attributes.function: account for remaining contributions to perturbative series exactly to all orders in alpha_s
treat double resummation of soft and collinear effects

relationships.target: Cracow Epiphany Conference on Precision Physics and Monte Carlos for LHC

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text outlines the organization of a paper on QED⊗QCD resummation, noting that QED contributions to structure functions are significant at the 0.3% level. It details the extension of YFS theory to QCD, presenting an exact cross-section formula for heavy boson production that isolates infrared divergences into residuals. The section emphasizes the exactness of the QCD resummation and its realization via Monte Carlo methods.

attributes.significance: almost half of the error budget for ~1.0% theoretical precision

attributes.parton_level_reaction: q + q'bar → V + n(g) + X → lbar l' + n(g) + X

attributes.mechanism: Compensation between genuine non-Abelian IR virtual and real singularities

knowledge_units.context_summary: The QED⊗QCD resummation theory is derived by simultaneously exponentiating infrared terms from QCD and QED, resulting in a cross-section formula with combined residuals. The infrared algebra indicates that QCD corrections occur at a significantly earlier scale than QED corrections due to differences in coupling strengths and color factors. This exact representation allows for the calculation of threshold corrections and matching with parton shower Monte Carlo methods without double-counting.

attributes.derivation: simultaneous exponentiation of large IR terms in QCD and exact IR divergent terms in QED
attributes.application: precision LHC physics, heavy gauge boson production

relationships.target: double counting in parton shower MCs

attributes.definition: successive application of YFS expansion first for QCD and subsequently for QED
attributes.parameters: n hard gluons, m hard photons

attributes.derivation: determined from QCD analogs SUMIR(QCD) and DQCD via substitution of QED terms

attributes.color_factors: CA = Qf^2 for QED, CF for QCD
attributes.implication: QCD dominant corrections happen an order of magnitude earlier than QED corrections

attributes.utility: provides a good estimate of the size of interplay between higher order QED and QCD effects

knowledge_units.context_summary: The authors propose combining their exact YFS-style QED⊗QCD resummation with standard parton shower generators like HERWIG and PYTHIA to avoid double counting. They describe a method where DGLAP evolution factorizes collinear singularities, requiring the omission of gluon radiation below the factorization scale in the residuals. This approach allows for a systematic, order-by-order improvement of precision in LHC physics calculations.

attributes.function: factorizes terms involving powers of the big log Lc

relationships.target: largest pT of gluon emission in structure function

attributes.definition: largest pT of the gluon emission included in the structure function

attributes.constraint: omitted at scales below factorization scale µ

attributes.application: applied to cross section in equation (2)

relationships.target: quark mass mq or dimensional regularization

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text describes two methods for matching parton shower simulations with matrix element calculations in QED⊗QCD resummation. The first method uses pT matching to prevent double counting, while the second employs shower-subtracted residuals for higher accuracy across the full phase space. The authors also define the ratio of exponentiated to Born cross sections for precision heavy vector boson studies.

attributes.description: Matching of the shower from backward evolution with matrix elements in the QCED exponentiated cross section by restricting pT

attributes.calculation_method: Computed by expanding the shower formula, exponents in (2), and residuals, and matching coefficients of powers of αnαm s to exact results
attributes.accuracy: Improved compared with pT matching procedure

relationships.target: exact O(α) luminosity Bhabha process at DAPHNE energies
backward evolution of the initial partons
Set a paradigm for precision heavy vector boson studies

attributes.derivation: Obtained from formula (4) by substituting dˆσBorn for dˆσexp

attributes.convergence: Much more convergent than its analog in LEP physics for electroweak theory

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text defines the QED⊗QCD exponent and associated YFS functions for calculating threshold corrections in heavy gauge boson production. It presents specific numerical ratios for LHC and Tevatron environments, demonstrating that QED effects are approximately 0.3%. The authors conclude that this level of precision is necessary for LHC theory predictions and that the method allows for Monte Carlo realization using HERWIG and PYTHIA.

attributes.definition: Logarithmic term defined when µ is the factorization scale

attributes.necessity: needed for LHC theory predictions at ≲1%

relationships.target: simultaneous exponentiation of QED and QCD
